newsitem.title: USA: USDA's Glickman defends CRP, Crown Butte proposal.
newsitem.headline: USDA's Glickman defends CRP, Crown Butte proposal.

text.p: U.S. Agriculture Secretary Dan Glickman Thursday defended the admininistration's plan to use Conservation Reserve Program (CRP) funds to pay Crown Butte not to mine near Yellowstone National Park, saying USDA had not expected to enroll all the acres allowed for CRP this year.
White House budget assumptions were that CRP contracts would be written this year on 19 million acres.

Glickman told the House Appropriations Interior subcommittee the plan to defer CRP sign-up of two million acres was made "under the theory you probably would have great difficulty signing up 19 million acres in fiscal 1998."
"The acreage could be deferred into the following years or years without disturbing the total amount of acres that would ultimately be coming in to the CRP," Glickman added.

He said USDA believed it would take a few years to build up to the 36.4 million acres goal for the revamped program primarily because the new rental rates were based on local rates and that would deter some producers from re-enrolling.

"Even with the increased interest, the folks who project indicate it's going to take us three to four years to get all the land in, that's why there was a feeling you could move two million acres...," he told reporters after the hearing.
That said, Glickman noted the proposal was driven by budget concerns and acknowledged concern expressed on Capitol Hill.
Panel chairman Rep. Ralph Regula, Ohio Republican, told Glickman the plan had caused "great distress" in the farm community.
"I think we're going to have a good debate on it...to see if it's good policy. I think it's not," Regula said.

Meanwhile, Senators Richard Lugar, Indiana Republican and Tom Harkin, Iowa Democrat, released a letter to Glickman dated March 19 urging USDA to operate the program carefully to ensure only the most environmentally sensitive lands were enrolled.
